title: Telemetry sleuth workshop — Request log timeline (Heliosware)
summary: Deep technical walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, request log timeline and error forensics for Heliosware's inference platform. Covered KV cache fallbacks, request correlation, VPC/SSO requirements, and proposed a scoped pilot. Agreed next steps: send security pack, run a 1-week hosted pilot with synthetic workload, and schedule a benchmark session with metrics sheet.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-12 UTC — 15:00
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonas (Redwood Product), Marta (Heliosware SRE), Liam (Heliosware Head of Platform), Jian (CTO), Sofia (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be rough) : quick run through of console traces, showed request timeline and how fallback triggers when KV cash (sic) misses; discussed encryption and VPC setup, ended with pilot actions.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros, we'll do a targeted walk through of the Console trace timeline and then deep dive into a couple of error paths you sent over.
[00:12] Marta: Hi, thanks. We have a noisy production spike last week and we saw requests time out, and then some inference responses seem to fall back to a cheaper model and degraded the UX.
[00:23] Ethan: Right, that sounds like the routing fallback policy — we can show how the Console surfaces that. Also we'll show the KV cache and prefix caching behavior that can cause cold-start stutter.
[00:35] Liam: Important for us — we need to know where to look in logs for correlation across Redis, ingress, and infer nodes.
[00:46] Priya: Great, we put together a trace export and a sample request id you sent in the deck. I'll load that so you can see the timeline.
[01:10] Jonas: Quick note — some product names in the transcript may be misheard, e.g., 'Redwood Opti-mize' flagged in auto-caption, but it's Redwood Optimize.
[01:22] [screen share starts] Ethan: Ok loading the trace. At the top is the request timeline — you can see ingress -> routing -> model call -> KV cache hit/miss, then fallback. Timestamped spans every 200ms, approximate.
[01:45] Marta: I see a long gap between routing decision and model start, what's that gap?
[01:50] Ethan: That's the wait for a GPU slot — in shared hosted mode we batch, so depending on concurrency you can see queuing. We annotate that as 'queue-wait' in the trace.
[02:12] Samira: For Heliosware, given your SLOs, we might recommend a Dedicated pool to reduce queue latency — but we also want to show you how to use continuous batching and a smaller quantized variant to reduce cost.
[02:34] Jian: Can you show where the fallback trigger shows up? We saw responses apparently coming from a 'smaller' model.
[02:42] Ethan: Yep — here's the routing span that includes policy: latency_threshold=350ms, cost_threshold flag, fallback_model=small-v1. You can filter traces where routing.took > 350ms and then see a downstream call to small-v1.
[03:05] Marta: The trace shows a KV missing earlier — the 'KV cash' sometimes shows as K V cache in captions — that miss caused model to recompute embeddings which added 150ms.
[03:20] Priya: Also we annotate the request with a hash of the prompt prefix so you can inspect prefix caching effectiveness.
[03:40] Liam: How do we stitch request logs from our ingress to Redwood's trace? We have egress IP/nat and internal request ids.
[03:55] Ethan: We recommend attaching your internal request_id to the Redwood request metadata header x-helio-req-id; Console will show it as the correlation id. If you can't change headers, we support a post-hoc log-stitching by uploading a CSV map.
[04:20] Sofia: Security question — does the trace export include any PII or prompt text in plain form? We need to know for compliance.
[04:32] Samira: Good q. By default, Console shows the prompt text in the UI for debugging, but exports can be redacted. We also support field-level redaction and encryption at rest via customer-managed KMS (HSM option) in Private deployments.
[04:58] Sofia: And SSO/SCIM — we want SAML SSO and SAML provisioning to map roles.
[05:10] Samira: Yes — SSO via SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC can be tied to groups. We'll include the SAML docs in the security pack.
[05:22] [10 min walkthrough of UI omitted in transcript excerpt]
[15:10] Ethan: Back to the log — here's an error span where the model returned a 429 upstream. Console surfaces that as 'rate-limit' and we show the token-level breakdown so you can see which token groups caused spikes.
[15:33] Marta: The 429s correspond to an ETL job that ran on a schedule, we didn't anticipate the burst. Can Console alert on that?
[15:40] Priya: Yes, you can set alerting on error rates per route or per model, and we also show a heatmap of request qps per minute.
[16:05] Liam: For the pilot, we want metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens per call, cost per 1k tokens, and cache hit rate. Can you provide those?
[16:20] Ethan: We'll deliver a benchmark sheet with those columns and examples from a synthetic load. We'll also include expected unit economics for different batch sizes and quantization profiles.
[16:40] Marta: Show me an example of how a KV cache miss looks across the timeline.
[16:48] Ethan: Here — you see a KV miss span that adds 120–160ms; the SQL-like query to prefix kv shows as a child span. In older captions this was labeled "prefix cache lookup" but sometimes transcribed as prefix 'cash' — ignore that.
[17:10] Samira: If you want to avoid the miss penalty, we can pre-warm the cache for hot prefixes during your nightly batch; we can put that in the pilot scope.
[17:29] Jian: We run in a VPC and need to ensure traffic never traverses public internet. How do Private deployments look?
[17:38] Ethan: Private deployments give you a control plane in your VPC or on-prem. You get customer-managed KMS, audit logs to your SIEM, and a local egress path. We'll share our architecture doc.
[17:55] Sofia: Audit log retention — minimums and exports?
[18:02] Samira: We support configurable retention; enterprise customers can push logs to S3 in their account for long-term retention and tie to SIEM.
[18:20] [small cross talk; someone drops a noise]
[18:40] Priya: Ok pulling up the sample trace you sent — request id 0a3f-... I can see the exact sequence: ingress -> auth -> route -> batch queue -> model-start -> fallback model call -> response.
[19:05] Marta: We notice response bodies are truncated sometimes. Is that the console or the client?
[19:13] Ethan: Console shows the full server response; truncation often happens at the client SDK level if the SDK times out or if streaming is cut. We can show your SDK timeout values during pilot.
[19:32] Liam: About cost, if we go dedicated how do burst windows work? We have heavy peaks.
[19:40] Samira: Dedicated pools can have burst capacity and autoscale policies; you can also run mixed strategy — pinned capacity for baseline and hosted for overflow. The Console traces will indicate which pool served each request.
[20:05] Jian: Curious about routing heuristics — do you support model-awareness per route? Like certain routes always prefer a quantized variant?
[20:12] Ethan: Yes, routing policies support per-route pins and model families; we can set soft-preference rules to prefer quantized models for non-critical routes.
[20:40] Marta: Can we get an example alert rule for cache degradation?
[20:46] Priya: Example: Alert if cache hit rate < 75% for 5-min window AND error rate > 1% on the same route. We'll drop the concrete rule in the workbook.
[21:05] [30 min mark — deeper Q&A on edge cases]
[30:20] Ethan: Here's a tricky scenario: when a chain of tool calls is happening and one tool fails, Console shows both the tool-error span and the parent request error. We expose both so you can triage whether it's internal model timeout or downstream tool failure.
[30:45] Marta: That matches what we saw — a third-party search call timed out causing downstream model to generate a fallback.
[31:00] Samira: In the Console you can click into the request timeline and 'jump to logs' which stitches together your application logs if you've uploaded log pointers; we can do that for Heliosware.
[31:24] Liam: About privacy, can exported traces redact prompt content but keep timings? We need to preserve timing correlation for triage without exposing PII.
[31:33] Ethan: Yes, redaction profiles let you redact prompt_text but keep span metadata and durations — we'll include the redact config example.
[32:00] Marta: Ok pilot scope — we'd like a 1-week hosted pilot with our production-like synthetic traffic, simulating spikes. Evaluate: p95 <= 500ms, cache hit >= 80%, and no user-visible fallbacks more than 0.5% of requests.
[32:22] Samira: Sounds good. We'll propose a pilot worksheet and success criteria.
[32:30] Jian: SLA questions — uptime, response time guarantees?
[32:36] Samira: Hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency/uptime commitments. We'll include the Dedicated SLA doc in the packet.
[32:50] Sofia: One last security ask — we need to run an architecture review with our security team before pilot starts.
[32:58] Samira: Absolutely — we'll coordinate with your security team. We'll send available slots for an architecture review.
[33:12] [wrap-up and recaps] Samira: Quick recap — Samira will send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS notes) and SAML docs; Ethan will provide benchmark workbook and an example trace export; Heliosware will share sample request ids and confirm pilot criteria.
[33:33] Marta: Great, thanks. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[33:38] Ethan: No blockers — just access to sample traffic and to enable a test API key for the pilot.
[33:45] Liam: We'll get that to you.
[33:50] Samira: Ok we'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite for kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[34:00] [meeting ends — rest of the 54min used for side conversations and scheduling that didn't capture well in transcript]

Notes on transcription quality: speakers overlapped at times, names occasionally misattributed by auto-caption. Some technical terms transcribed oddly (KV cash, Redwood Opti-mize), please rely on transcript context.
